Marissa / Neha —

I've reviewed the questionnaire. Key points / suggested facts to include in the reply:

- Data classification: We recommend we state that Redwood classifies data into three categories: Non-PII (metadata), PII (identifiers: names, emails, phone numbers), and Sensitive PII (health-related content when explicitly provided). We should make clear that customers can opt to mask or tokenize fields before sending.

- Subprocessors: For the inference path we typically list: GPU hosts (cloud provider managed), a managed metrics/observability provider, a managed KV cache (for short-lived prefix cache), and a hosted object store for model artifacts/backups. We should call out that telemetry is aggregated and pseudonymized; no customer plaintext PII is sent to analytics.

- Transfer mechanism: For EU data we operate under the EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) when data is transferred to US-backed processing. We can also support customer-specific SCC deployment language via DPA exhibit. If the customer requires, we support on-prem or EU-only Dedicated deployments.

- Key management & encryption: We encrypt at rest and in transit by default. Customers on Dedicated/Private can bring-your-own-key (BYOK) or integrate with their KMS/HSM. We do not have access to customer KMS keys unless explicitly provisioned for support (rare; logged).

- Retention/deletion: Default: logs/metrics 90 days, inference KV cache ephemeral (minutes-hours depending on workload), hardened backups 30 days unless customer-specified retention longer. API and Console provide explicit record deletion hooks; we can respond to deletion requests under DPA timelines.

Attachments: I've uploaded a simplified dataflow diagram to our privacy drive and attached a PNG here that highlights ingress → inference runtime → KV cache → model store → backups. Please check the highlights and tell me if Nimbus needs anything more granular.

Action items I propose:
- Neha: provide suggested language for the DPA amendment (subprocessor notification window, audit rights)
- Marissa: confirm what Nimbus specifically considers "health data" for their mapping (PHI vs general identifiers) — they might want tighter retention limits.

Regards,

Thanks Kim — adding a few concrete answers you can paste into the questionnaire and into the DPA exhibit. I'm including suggested wording where Nimbus will want legally precise text.

1) Subprocessors & access to plaintext PII
- List: Cloud GPU provider (inference compute), Managed KV cache provider (short-lived caches), Metrics/observability provider, Object storage backup provider, CDN (if used).
- Access: Only the cloud GPU provider and object storage may persist encrypted artefacts; plaintext PII is not stored by analytics providers. Access to plaintext customer data by any Redwood subprocessors requires documented justification and is subject to our least-privilege controls and role-based access (RBAC).

Suggested DPA clause (subprocessor notification):
"Vendor will provide Customer with notice of any new subprocessor at least 30 calendar days prior to the subprocessor processing Customer Personal Data, and will provide an opportunity for Customer to object to the new subprocessor within 15 calendar days."

2) Cross-border transfers and safeguards
- Default mechanism: EU Commission Standard Contractual Clauses + supplementary technical measures (encryption at rest/in transit; where necessary, additional contractual assurances available on request).
- Alternative: For customers requiring no transfers to the US, Redwood can deploy into an EU-only Dedicated environment (requires order form).

3) Data flows & retention
- Ingest: Customer → Redwood edge (TLS)
- Short-term cache: KV cache (ephemeral, typically minutes-hours)
- Inference runtime: transient tokenized context stored only for the duration of the request unless a customer elects session persistence
- Backups/artifacts: encrypted, retention default 30 days for backups, extendable by customer request.

4) Evidence & audits
- SOC 2 Type II available; ISO 27001 in progress (expected Q4 2026). We can provide redacted logs or a scoped SOC2 report under NDA.

I'm comfortable with Kim's suggested text. Marissa — I edited the questionnaire PDF and saved as answered-questionnaire-nimbus-20261023.pdf (attached). If you want, I can send the answers directly to Alex and Lydia this afternoon with the diagram.
